title: Exhibit complex rank-seven P104 approximations below the real 1/4 floor (no κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Complex coefficients beat the sharp real rank-seven quarter-error floor for the fixed P104 Gram matrix. For `K=RR^T/2`, the explicit vector
`z=(5-5i,3+9i,5-5i,7,5-5i,-1-4i,-7,-7)`
gives `D=I-zz*/404` and `C=RDR^T/2` with **complex rank seven** and exact maximum complex entry error **25/101 < 1/4**. A second retained witness achieves **1205/4912**, with gap **23/4912** below 1/4. Neither witness is claimed optimal.

D is a Hermitian positive contractive orthogonal projector. C satisfies `0<=C<=K`, not an ambient `C<=I` claim. Its real part has rank eight, so this answers the complex-field question in #6191 without contradicting that real theorem or giving a seven-real-mode implementation.

Scoped exact finite construction and written proof; **no new κ or selected-frontier change**. Odd denominators remain, and no Gaussian-dyadic/native implementation, caller installation, residual correction, ownership/restoration or complete paid/target invoice is supplied.

## Task and overlap

Canonical main refreshed first and before submission at `a5bff3bf133e482541c09eba4e773884bdb2b1b7`, priority revision 8. Task `coverage-law-change`, scope key `2bf6355a8dd01ca324fb`, **scope changed** to this algebraic approximation question; the original supplier acceptance gate remains unmet.

[Canonical advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19275237). Nearest predecessors:
- #6191, `be3fc854aa380b3d81e134ce9a4282468e4fa999`: sharp real theorem and released complex question; still pending.
- Nick Petalas's #6183, `eaf77790466f34b86ce72080e3ec690e26dfacab`: contractive question, real projection and retained root data.
- Matarener's #6166, `096938513138868f0ed27639061f1a5054900f96`: cited physical P104-to-D8 identification and omitted lines. That identification is not newly audited.

The local helper covered 30/8623 notes, with no usable remote cache. Live checks covered the newest 20 PRs, newest 15 handoffs and all-state P104/complex/rank, 6191 and Gram/contractive searches; the relevant search and source heads were refreshed before submission. No competing complex witness appeared in those bounded results. #6194 studies a different paid frame-graph projection objective. No exhaustive novelty claim.

## Validation

Publication head: `369ad15647ad0df0b0ef6f4fcb060509b67f1823`. CPython 3.12.14, macOS arm64, standard library only.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-complex-rank-seven
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-complex-rank-seven --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Both separately written checkers pass normal and optimized registered replays. Each checks all **21,632** residual entries across the two full matrices. The primary checks nine hypothesis controls and all three pinned predecessor inputs; the independent Fraction-based checker uses a different root order and independently checks complex rank-seven and real-part rank-eight minors, plus four projector controls. Three primary source-corruption controls and the independent root-data corruption control reject.

Committed bytes/modes, declared source ancestry and official export integrity pass. All four direct commands pass in a fresh read-only, Git-free export with empty PATH. Normal/optimized outputs agree and all eleven exported files retain their bytes and modes. A separate AI proof audit found no blockers.

The rank/error claims combine written projection/rank arguments with complete exact finite arithmetic, not floating-point optimization or a formal proof kernel. Discovery search is not needed for replay. No further optimization was run this round.

Not run: selected scientific cold replay, physical/native/caller replay, Lean, Docker or independent human review. Binding-only orientation was reused after confirming 1227 bound inputs unchanged; this is not a fresh scientific replay. Hosted CI is pending at submission.

## Open next questions

[README and structured questions](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/369ad15647ad0df0b0ef6f4fcb060509b67f1823/research/p104-complex-rank-seven/README.md) identify two next gates: one exact Gaussian-dyadic projector that beats 1/4, and one actual caller whose complete residual-correction/restoration bill is favorable. The present witnesses supply neither. Lower coefficient error alone is not a paid-work saving.
